questions.stem: A 22-year-old woman requested HPV vaccination. She reported sex with both men and women with five sex partners in the last year. She was tested annually for STIs and HIV . She tested positive for chlamydia 2 years ago and was treated with azithromycin 1 g. All STI tests were negative at her last screening 6 months ago.
questions.lead_in: What is the most appropriate action?

options.text: Do not vaccinate. Explain that she has likely already been exposed to HPV , and vaccination is not indicated
Do not vaccinate. She is too old to receive the vaccine
Test for presence of HPV using a vaginal swab. If HPV is present, do not vaccinate

questions.explanation: Vaccinate with three-dose series HPV vaccination is recommended for adolescents age 11 or 12 years. Vaccination is also recommended for females between the ages of 13 and 26 and for males between the ages of 13 through 21 who were not adequately vaccinated previously. HPV vaccination is also recommended for gay, bisexual, and other men who have sex with men, transgender people, and those with some immunocompromising conditions between ages 22 and 26 years, if inadequately vaccinated in the past. The vaccine should be administered regardless of history of exposure.

parts.text: What is the only indication for HPV PCR testing for cervical specimens in Canada?

questions.model_answer: Reflex HPV testing to triage cervical cytology results reported as ASC-US (atypical squamous cells of undetermined significance) - this has historically been the only indication funded/approved for HPV PCR testing on cervical specimens in Canada.
questions.beyond_mandell: Canadian provincial cervical screening program policy (moving toward primary HPV screening in some provinces).

questions.question: HPV serotypes

parts.text: Which 2 serotypes of HPV are responsible for 70-80% of genital cancers?
Which 2 serotypes are responsible for 90% of anogenital warts?
Which 2 serotypes are responsible for most respiratory papillomatosis?

questions.model_answer:
a) HPV-16 and HPV-18 cause 70-80% of genital cancers.
b) HPV-6 and HPV-11 cause ~90% of anogenital warts.
c) HPV-6 and HPV-11 cause most cases of recurrent respiratory papillomatosis.

questions.question: Fill the table on HPV vaccine. **immunocompromised or ≥15yo get 3 doses

parts.text: For each HPV vaccine type (Bivalent, Quadrivalent), state: serogroups covered, number of doses, and whether licensed for males, females, or both.

questions.model_answer:
Bivalent HPV vaccine (Cervarix): covers HPV 16 and 18; given as 2 doses (ages 9-14) or 3 doses (age ≥15 or immunocompromised at any age); licensed for females only.
Quadrivalent HPV vaccine (Gardasil): covers HPV 6, 11, 16, and 18; given as 2 doses (ages 9-14) or 3 doses (age ≥15 or immunocompromised at any age); licensed for both males and females.
questions.beyond_mandell: NACI/Canadian Immunization Guide HPV vaccine chapter.

What are the 2 serotypes responsible for condylomata acuminata?
For laryngeal papillomatosis?
Complete the table of vaccines (Bivalent/Quadrivalent, Vaccine, Serotypes covered, Number of doses, Men/Women/Both) for Bivalent and Quadrivalent

questions.model_answer:
a) HPV-16 and HPV-18 cause 70-90% of HPV-related malignancies.
b) HPV-6 and HPV-11 cause condylomata acuminata.

questions.question:
Q26 (2007)
Girl with condylomata wants to know about her risk of having an abnormal PAP test.

parts.text: A.  What should you answer her?

cohort_answer.text: The presence of external genital warts may indicate the existence of cervical HPV squamous epithelial lesions, including CIN bc common risk factor (sexual activity)

parts.text: B. Method of detection

cohort_answer.text: *Male anal paps guideline? Initiate screening with Pap (cytology) at age 21 (or 25) if any Hx of any sexual activity. Every 3 years if no abnormality. Same for pregnancy, WSW, HPV-vaccinated, subtotal-hysterectomy, transgender men. Annual testing for Hx of HSIL, cervical cancer, HIV+ or immunosuppressed. Discontinue at 70 yo if 3 or more negative cytology in previous 10 years. No routine HPV immunohistochemical testing -> only if abnormality on cytology (vs American guidelines)

parts.text: Name 6 different viruses and an associated malignancy with each one

questions.model_answer: (1) Human papillomavirus - cervical/anogenital/oropharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma (2) Hepatitis B virus - hepatocellular carcinoma (3) Hepatitis C virus - hepatocellular carcinoma (4) Epstein-Barr virus - Burkitt lymphoma, Hodgkin lymphoma, nasopharyngeal carcinoma, or PTLD (5) HHV-8 (KSHV) - Kaposi sarcoma (6) HTLV-1 - adult T-cell leukemia/lymphoma.
questions.cites: Mandell pp. 1884-1889 (EBV malignancies); others beyond this chapter

parts.text: Name 6 different viruses that cause cancer and what type of cancer?

questions.model_answer: (1) Human papillomavirus (HPV) - cervical, anal, vulvar/vaginal/penile, and oropharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma. (2) Hepatitis B virus - hepatocellular carcinoma. (3) Hepatitis C virus - hepatocellular carcinoma. (4) Epstein-Barr virus - Burkitt lymphoma, nasopharyngeal carcinoma, Hodgkin lymphoma. (5) Human herpesvirus-8 (HHV-8/KSHV) - Kaposi sarcoma, primary effusion lymphoma, multicentric Castleman disease. (6) Human T-lymphotropic virus type 1 (HTLV-1) - adult T-cell leukemia/lymphoma (Merkel cell polyomavirus causing Merkel cell carcinoma is another acceptable answer).
questions.cites: Mandell pp. 1917-1920 (HPV); other viruses beyond this chapter

parts.text: What are 6 viruses that cause cancer and a cancer they cause? (presented as a chart: Virus / Associated cancer)

questions.model_answer: Virus / Associated cancer: (1) HPV - cervical/anogenital/oropharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma (2) Hepatitis B virus - hepatocellular carcinoma (3) Hepatitis C virus - hepatocellular carcinoma (4) Epstein-Barr virus - Burkitt lymphoma/nasopharyngeal carcinoma/Hodgkin lymphoma (5) HHV-8 - Kaposi sarcoma (6) HTLV-1 - adult T-cell leukemia/lymphoma.

questions.question: Which malignancies are associated with the following organisms:

parts.text: Hepatitis C virus
HPV
Schistosoma haematobium
Clonorchis
H. pylori
HHV8

questions.model_answer:
Hepatitis C virus - hepatocellular carcinoma (and B-cell non-Hodgkin lymphoma).
HPV - cervical, anal, vulvar/vaginal/penile, and oropharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma.
Schistosoma haematobium - bladder (squamous cell) carcinoma.
Clonorchis (sinensis) - cholangiocarcinoma.
H. pylori - gastric adenocarcinoma and gastric MALT lymphoma.
HHV-8 - Kaposi sarcoma, primary effusion lymphoma, multicentric Castleman disease.
